evals.name: warsh-support-flutter
evals.prompt: My Quran app currently supports Hafs only. It's a Flutter app with a local SQLite database of ayahs (columns: surah, ayah_number, text, page) and a bookmarks table (surah, ayah_number, created_at). I want to add support for Warsh (riwayat Warsh an Nafi'). Write a concrete migration plan to plan.md covering: data model changes, where to get the Warsh text, fonts, audio recitation, and what could silently break if we do it naively.
evals.expected_output: A plan that handles the different ayah counting (never assumes Hafs numbering works for Warsh), uses cross-riwayah mapping/anchoring, scopes bookmarks to a mushaf, sources verified Warsh text, requires a Warsh-specific font, and ties audio to the riwayah.
assertions: Plan accounts for the different ayah numbering between Hafs and Warsh (counting systems, merged/split ayahs, or cross-riwayah mapping) instead of reusing Hafs ayah_number for Warsh
Bookmarks/user data become mushaf/riwayah-scoped (schema records which riwayah each bookmark belongs to)
Warsh text is sourced from a verified published source, not produced by programmatically transforming the Hafs text
Plan requires a Warsh-specific Quranic font rather than reusing the Hafs font
Audio is tied to the riwayah: Warsh text is paired with Warsh reciters, not arbitrary Hafs recordings

evals.name: wordpress-ayah-embed
evals.prompt: i have a wordpress blog about tafsir in arabic. i want to show quran verses inside my posts nicely, and let readers tap a verse to read its tafsir without leaving the post. i really don't want to build a backend or maintain a plugin. what's the easiest way? give me concrete steps and paste-able code. write the answer to answer.md
evals.expected_output: Recommends an embed/oEmbed approach (e.g., QuranPedia embed widget) with paste-able snippets, complete ayahs in a proper Quranic font, tafsir on tap, no custom backend.
assertions: Recommends an embed/oEmbed solution that requires no custom backend or plugin maintenance (e.g., an embeddable Quran widget service), rather than building one
Provides paste-able code (script tag, iframe, embeddable link, or oEmbed URL) that works inside WordPress posts
Tafsir is reachable on tap/click without leaving the post, per the requirement
Verses render complete and in a proper Quranic font — no hand-typed or truncated Quranic text in the snippets

evals.name: hifz-app-design
evals.prompt: Design the core feature set and data model for a Quran memorization (hifz) app for mobile. Users typically memorize under a teacher. Include how the app would automatically check the user's recitation, and be honest about what automation can and cannot do. Deliver a design doc as design.md.
evals.expected_output: A design grounded in traditional hifz practice (revision tiers/spaced repetition with a review queue, page-based progress), mutashabihat confusion handling, offline-first, verse-recognition-based checking with honest limits (no tajweed-grading claims), teacher workflow support.
assertions: Review system is structured — spaced repetition and/or traditional revision tiers (new lesson / recent / long-term revision) with a review queue, not just a list of memorized surahs
Mutashabihat (similar-verse confusion) is handled explicitly as a feature or data concern
Recitation checking is honest: verse-recognition/ASR with confidence limits, no claim of reliable automatic tajweed grading, and the teacher stays in the loop
Data model tracks progress by page or ayah-range with mushaf context, and mistakes at word or ayah level
Core memorization flows work offline

evals.name: interactive-mushaf-word-highlight
evals.prompt: I'm building an Android and iOS Quran app. I want the real printed mushaf pages, and while a reciter plays the current word should light up and users should be able to tap any word to see its meaning. Which building blocks should I use, and how do they fit together? Write the plan to plan.md.
evals.expected_output: Recommends Quran.ws quran-svg-elements + quran-engine (+ quran-text for word identity), not quran-svg alone, notes Hafs-only coverage and Beta maturity, separates word timing/audio and meanings as outside the blocks, and pins versions and checks licences.
assertions: Chooses quran-svg-elements and quran-engine for word-level interaction rather than quran-svg (ayah polygons only)
States that quran-svg-elements currently covers Hafs only, or otherwise flags coverage limits
Sources word-level audio timings and word meanings from outside the Quran.ws blocks (for example Quran Foundation or QUL)
Mentions checking licences or pinning versions of the blocks or their data

evals.name: tajweed-reader
evals.prompt: Add tajweed colouring to my web Quran reader. It already shows Hafs text from my own JSON file. What's the cleanest way? Give concrete steps and code, and write it to answer.md.
evals.expected_output: Uses quran-tajweed annotation spans over unchanged text, checks the app's text matches the edition the spans were measured on, does not alter the Quranic text or use regex rules, and does not present colours as a substitute for a teacher.
assertions: Uses precomputed tajweed annotation spans (for example quran-tajweed) applied over the unchanged text, rather than editing the text or writing regex detection from scratch
Verifies the app's text matches the edition the spans were computed against, or explains why offsets would drift
Renders colour as a presentation layer without stripping or altering diacritics or waqf marks
Does not hand-type Quranic text in the code samples

evals.name: warsh-tafsir-join
evals.prompt: My app shows Warsh text and joins each ayah to a tafsir table keyed by (surah, ayah) in Hafs numbering. Users report that some Warsh ayahs show the wrong tafsir or none. Explain what is going wrong and how to fix it with concrete code. Write it to answer.md.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the counting-system mismatch, recommends the qiraat-ayah-map conversion through the Kufan hub handling split/merged ayahs (one ayah may map to a range), and notes keys need a counting system.
assertions: Identifies different ayah numbering between Warsh and Hafs (splits and merges) as the cause
Converts through a maintained mapping dataset (for example qiraat-ayah-map) instead of hand-written offsets
Handles one Warsh ayah mapping to a range of Hafs ayahs, or the reverse
Recommends scoping ayah keys by counting system or riwayah

evals.name: ornament-licence-check
evals.prompt: I'm making a paid Quran study app and want nice surah header banners and ayah number markers in the style of the printed mushaf. Where should I get them and is there anything I must check before shipping? Write to answer.md.
evals.expected_output: Points to quran-assets, tells the user to read each asset's licence and status in catalog.json, warns that scan-derived ornaments are provisional CC BY-NC-SA and unsuitable for a paid app without clearance, and prefers OFL font-derived markers.
assertions: Recommends quran-assets (or equivalent open, recolourable SVG source) instead of redrawing or copying from another app
Says to check each asset's licence and status before shipping, for example in catalog.json
Warns that some assets are non-commercial or provisional and not safe for a paid app without clearance
Suggests OFL-licensed assets as the safe choice for commercial use
